Row.description: Places children side by side. Wraps on narrow screens unless `wrap` is false. padding.description: The space inside the edge, around the children, as a step of the theme's spacing scale (`--sf-space-<step>`), or "none". Defaults to "none".

Grid.description: Lays children out in columns that wrap onto new rows. Use it for dashboards: a row of numbers, then charts side by side. Columns are equal unless `widths` gives each its share, as when a person resizes them by hand. Children in a row are stretched to the tallest one; set `align: "start"` when the row mixes content of different heights, such as a chart beside a form, so each keeps its own height. `gap` is a step of the theme's spacing scale, between rows and columns alike.

SideNav.description: Navigation down the side of a surface: groups of items, with the current one marked. A person can fold it away: it then keeps only a slim strip for its menu button, which slides it back in over the surface (never over anything outside it). In a narrow surface or on a narrow screen it is always folded. An item with `href` is a link (http and https only); one without sends the event with its `id`. Bind `current` to a data path to mark the item for what is showing.

Form.description: A form that checks what a person enters and submits it. Give the fields and their rules; the form draws a labelled input for each, shows errors beside them and sends nothing while any is wrong. A field with `visibleWhen: { field, equals }` is asked for only once another field holds that value. When the page has a forms backend, values go to the form with this `formId` there (the backend decides where they are stored; you never name a table); either way your event receives them. Use it instead of loose inputs and a Button whenever values must be checked or kept.
